name: comp-482
title: Expandable Rows Table
description: A dark account table where rows carrying a note show a chevron in the first column. Pressing it drops a full-width sub-row with an info icon and the note text; a checkbox column selects rows separately.
use: Each record carries a short note that should stay hidden until someone asks to read it.
avoid: Notes are long single paragraphs, so an open row pushes everything below it down a long way.
a11y: The expander is a labelled button reporting aria-expanded, and checkboxes are labelled; note text has no heading of its own. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A black table led by a narrow chevron column and a checkbox column, then bold names, emails, flag emojis with cities, rounded status pills and right-aligned balances. Open rows add a lighter strip containing a small info glyph and a paragraph.
behaves: Clicking a row's downward chevron unfolds a sub-row of note text and flips the chevron upward; clicking again folds it away. Rows without a note have no chevron, and the checkboxes tick independently of expansion.
customise: Rows load from a remote JSON while columns and the note sub-row are written in the file; new fields or a different note layout mean editing the source.
weight: moderate: A table library over five remote rows adds one sub-row on demand; no animation loop.
demo: Five people with flags, status pills and balances; one note about a quarterly performance review.
issues: The first column is blank for rows without a note, so the chevrons look uneven.
The caption credits the table library instead of describing the example.
Open notes appear instantly with no height animation, so the table jumps.
polishWhy: Clean sub-row with an info icon and roomy spacing; a library caption and uneven expander column.
